newsitem.title: UK: London gold teeters on verge of critical support.
newsitem.headline: London gold teeters on verge of critical support.

text.p: Gold threatened to topple to fresh lows for the year on Friday after a week of pummelling from all quarters, dealers said.
"The market looks weak and vulnerable. Everyone is having a go," a dealer said. A spate of selling this week has been linked to gold producers, a European central bank and investment funds.
Bullion fixed at $377.20 an ounce, off $2.30 from the previous fixing on Thursday afternoon and down more than $5.00 since the start of the week.
Gold prices could test support just below $377.00 an ounce amid an overwhelmingly bearish market mood, analysts said.
"At the moment gold is perilously close to key support at $376.90," brokers GNI said in a report, referring to the 18-month low gold hit at the start of October.
"If this goes the price could drop to $370 pretty quickly," the report added.
But some dealers said it would likely find decent support here and consolidate in a new, lower range for the time being.

Early trading was quiet with many European markets closed for All Saints Day holiday. The market was expected to hold off on big moves until after U.S. jobs data were released later in the day, dealers said.
U.S. economic news earlier this week suggested little threat of inflation, further diminishing investor interest in the precious metals, a traditional hedge against price rises.
Ironically, the cost of borrowing gold surged higher this week, particularly three-month gold lease rates, which indicated that supplies of metal available for borrowing were tight.
The expectation that gold miners planned to sell more metal in the near term was behind the move, dealers said.
Producers typically sell gold which they have not yet mined by borrowing metal from central banks to sell. They pay the bank back once their own gold has been mined and refined.
The other precious metals shared gold's fragile hold on nearby support levels.
Silver dropped six cents overnight to trade at $4.79/$4.80 an ounce. A break lower pointed to the $4.70 an ounce level, eventually targetting levels as low as $4.50, analysts said.
Platinum, having slid below the psychological $380 an ounce level overnight, was trading at $379.00/$380.00, down $1.50. Its fate was likely linked with gold's, dealers said.
"If gold goes, platinum may follow it," a dealer said.
Its sister metal palladium was unchanged at $115.50/$116.50.
